note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: CORRECTION (Oct 21): no US shutdown — Trump signed the CR Sept 2, funded through Dec 11; Sept jobs/CPI/PPI/housing all printed on schedule. France: OAT-Bund ~173bp (Reuters, Oct 22 — widest since Nov 2011; 10Y OAT tested 5.14%); Macron banned Saturday's Lyon protests, troops deployed; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg → A1 widely expected); CDS at BBB territory. Revenue-section first reading Oct 27 (49.3 floated); Nov-5 cross-sector strike called. UK: Sep borrowing £24.5B miss (vs £23.9B), debt >£3T first time; Healey's first Budget Oct 28.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US: jobless claims BEAT 194K (vs 200K fcst; near 57-year lows); leading index flat beat (0.0% vs -0.2%); housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales record low) vs last week's retail/IP beats. UK: jobs beat (unemp 4.7%) + GDP +0.1% beat vs CBI orders -32 miss; GfK -24 big miss. Australia: flash PMIs big miss — composite 47.7, services 47.8 (first private-sector contraction in 5 months); employment -39.3K, unemp 4.7% five-year high. Canada: IPPI +2.0% beat, RMPI +4.8% beat. Japan: flash mfg 53.3 (7-month low) vs svc 52.0 up. EZ: consumer confidence -17.9 miss. Oct flash PMIs (Oct 23): France miss (mfg 49.3 vs 50.5 fcst, svc 48.4 vs 50.7, back in contraction), Germany comp 52.8 vs 53.3 fcst (mfg 54.2 beat), EZ comp 51.9 vs 52.7 (slowest in 4 months); UK comp 53.1 beat (vs 51.8 fcst, strongest since Feb) vs Sep retail sales -0.4% miss (vs -0.1% fcst). Canada retail sales (Aug) due 7:30am CT — five days before the Oct 28 BoC.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US CPI 3.7%, PPI hot; import prices +8.1% y/y (4-yr high); crude above $114 — energy re-acceleration risk. UK Sep CPI verified 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky) — locks the Nov-5 BoE hike; GfK inflation expectations highest since April. German Sep PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%). NZ Q3 CPI soft miss: 0.7% q/q, 3.7% y/y (below RBNZ's 3.9% proj, still above 1-3% target) — hike stayed ~98% priced. Japan national core CPI 2.1% inline (first above BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4%) — cements the December hike.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Oct 27-28 FOMC a hold at ~93% (CME FedWatch via FXStreet, Oct 23); December hike ~90%. BoC Oct 28 hike ~80-87% (LSEG/swap, Oct 22; BMO/RBC/Desjardins flipped hold→hike). RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~98% (Reuters Oct 22) — the soft NZ CPI didn't dent it; terminal 3.25-3.50% (ING). ECB Oct 29 hold virtually certain (~93-97%); December hike ~88-90%. BoE Nov 5 hike ~90-95%; December back-to-back ~48-61%. BoJ Oct 29-30 hold ~96%+; December hike ~80% (OIS). RBA Nov 2-3 hike ~44-50% (Hauser: ~50%; Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot). SNB Dec 10 ~50-50.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 13 report): all G10 signals neutral (0). Splits: hedge funds flipped AGAINST the yen while real money bets FOR it; hedge funds for the Aussie but real money strongly against. Funds strongly short CAD (added sharply) — squeeze risk if BoC hikes. No crowded-long unwind risk anywhere — the pain trade is two-sided. New CFTC report lands 3:30pm CT today.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Risk-off: Nasdaq -2.6% (worst since June) on AI-spending concerns (Meta -7%, AMD -8%, Nvidia -4%); 10Y -19bp to 4.956% (biggest one-day drop since Mar 2023) as investors fled to bonds; DXY ~101.52 near the 3-week low — no USD haven bid. The haven trade went to the yen (USD/JPY toward 156.3, strongest in 1+ months) and the franc. Brent above $114 (highest since May 4) on Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infra + NYT's US/Israel Iran-strike plans for after the Nov-3 midterms; Aramco evacuated Dhahran HQ (first since the Iran war began).
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent pushed above $114 (settled Thu $113.17, +4.0% — highest since May 4); WTI ~$99.5 (+2.4%). Energy-exporter tailwind (CAD, AUD); energy-importer tax (EUR, JPY). Gold ~$4,013-4,022 (-2.5% to -3%) — near the 3-month low despite risk-off, cross-market liquidation in the equity rout.
tot.title: Terms of trade
